**Option 3 (`--edge-weight-mode`) measured on two codebases: no consistent gain over `--resolution`**

On #942 I wrote that I'd look into the third option from this issue, `--edge-weight-mode` (down-weighting edges at high-degree nodes), and "open it as a real PR with tests if it holds up". I measured it on 0.9.71, on two codebases. It doesn't hold up as a new flag, so here are the measurements instead of a PR. Along the way, two other things came up: measurements on the open PR #2388 by keith-oak, and a bug in `--exclude-hubs`, now fixed in 0.9.73 (#3933).

## Summary

- **At the same number of communities, degree-based edge weighting gives no consistent improvement over `--resolution`.** Most differences are larger than the seed noise, but their sign changes with the graph and with the granularity. In the regime closest to the #919 symptom (about 20 communities on the #919 codebase), weighting gives lower modularity, a larger largest community and lower cohesion.
- **On `v8` today, `--resolution` barely reaches the final output**, because the split passes re-partition at the default 1.0. #2388 fixes that. I measured it and posted the numbers there (https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/2388#issuecomment-5926457601), including a side effect on the 25% oversize cap.

## Setup

- `graphifyy` 0.9.71 from PyPI (`v8` at [`d6eaa8a`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/tree/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a)). The code paths measured here are the same in 0.9.73: its only change to `cluster.py`, #3933, runs only with `--exclude-hubs`. Both partition backends are reported separately: Leiden via `graspologic-native` 1.3.1, and the networkx 3.7 Louvain fallback that runs without the `leiden` extra.
- Two public AST-only graphs (`graphify extract <dir> --code-only`, no LLM), loaded as `cluster-only` loads them (`build_from_json`, self-loops included):
  - **A:** the #919 codebase at its current state ([neo1777/marzio1777 @ `0aa0333`](https://github.com/neo1777/marzio1777/tree/0aa0333)), 626 nodes and 1,661 edges. The graph behind #919 was larger: the #934 reproducer shows 1,501 nodes, built with graphify 0.8.x.
  - **B:** graphify's own `graphify/` package at `d6eaa8a`, 3,182 nodes and 7,784 edges, 109 of them self-loops.
- Weight schemes, set on every edge before partitioning (d = degree):
  - `uniform` = 1 (graphify's AST weights are already 1.0, except 12 INFERRED edges at 0.8 on B);
  - `inverse-degree` = 1/√(d_u·d_v);
  - `inverse-log-degree` = 1/(ln(1+d_u)·ln(1+d_v));
  - `inverse-max-degree` = 1/max(d_u, d_v);
  - `structural-triangle` = (1 + common neighbours)/(1 + union of neighbours), a triangle-based control (see *Why*).
- 12 seeds per setting, 1–12. graphify fixes `seed=42`; I wrapped `graspologic_native.leiden` and networkx's `louvain_communities` so every partitioner call gets the injected seed. 11 resolutions from 0.25 to 8.
- Metrics, all computed on the **unweighted** graph:
  - modularity Q (at resolution 1);
  - the size of the largest community (at the same community count, a larger one is the #919 shape);
  - size-weighted cohesion (graphify's `cohesion_score`, over communities of 3+ nodes);
  - **hub pull**: for each node at or above the 99th degree percentile (9 nodes on A, 34 on B, a looser rule than `--exclude-hubs`, which takes nodes *above* it), the share of its neighbours that land in its own community, averaged over those hubs. It is **descriptive, not a quality score**. A hub's private members (e.g. the symbols a file `contains`) belong with it, while the #919 symptom is a hub absorbing neighbours from other subsystems, and this number counts both.
- ± is the population SD over the 12 seeds.

## Result 1: full `cluster()` at resolution 1.0 (uniform vs inverse-degree)

| graph | backend | scheme | communities | largest | Q | hub pull | cohesion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Leiden | uniform | 21.3 | 76.9 | 0.620 ± 0.005 | 0.438 | 0.113 |
| A | Leiden | inverse-degree | 27.5 | 64.2 | 0.605 ± 0.004 | 0.398 | 0.144 |
| A | Louvain | uniform | 21.2 | 79.4 | 0.617 ± 0.008 | 0.445 | 0.113 |
| A | Louvain | inverse-degree | 27.0 | 69.0 | 0.609 ± 0.004 | 0.413 | 0.141 |
| B | Leiden | uniform | 151.3 | 104.7 | 0.617 ± 0.009 | 0.316 | 0.135 |
| B | Leiden | inverse-degree | 318.3 | 76.7 | 0.547 ± 0.003 | 0.155 | 0.209 |
| B | Louvain | uniform | 148.4 | 136.0 | 0.625 ± 0.010 | 0.353 | 0.131 |
| B | Louvain | inverse-degree | 311.6 | 78.0 | 0.550 ± 0.001 | 0.155 | 0.205 |

(means over 12 seeds; ± shown for Q. `uniform` differs from graphify's own weights only on B's 12 INFERRED edges, so B's counts here differ slightly from those on #2388.)

At resolution 1.0, weighting gives more and smaller communities, lower Q, lower hub pull and higher cohesion. Raising the resolution does all of that too, so the fair comparison is at the same number of communities.

## Result 2: at the same number of communities (first-pass partitioner)

The final `cluster()` output isn't monotonic in resolution, because the split passes reshape it (see below), and that confounds a matched comparison. So this part calls the first-pass partitioner `graphify.cluster._partition` directly, on the graph `cluster()` partitions (isolates removed). There, the community count rises with resolution for every scheme and backend; the one exception is a 0.2-community dip at the low end on A with Louvain, within the seed noise. Each metric is interpolated linearly against the mean community count, between the two resolutions that bracket the target.

inverse-degree minus uniform (★ = |Δ| larger than √(SD₁² + SD₂²): a one-SD screen, not a significance test):

| graph | communities | backend | ΔQ | Δ largest | Δ hub pull |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 20 | Leiden | −0.031 ★ | +68.3 ★ | +0.092 ★ |
| A | 20 | Louvain | −0.030 ★ | +60.5 ★ | +0.093 ★ |
| A | 40 | Leiden | +0.010 ★ | +6.3 ★ | +0.062 ★ |
| A | 40 | Louvain | +0.010 ★ | +6.5 ★ | +0.043 ★ |
| B | 50 | Leiden | −0.009 ★ | −24.8 ★ | −0.054 ★ |
| B | 50 | Louvain | −0.011 ★ | −35.1 ★ | −0.072 ★ |
| B | 100 | Leiden | +0.009 ★ | +0.2 | +0.001 |
| B | 100 | Louvain | +0.007 ★ | −1.5 | −0.001 |

The other three weightings also change the sign of ΔQ with the granularity, and give a larger largest community in 23 of their 24 cells, so the smaller largest community on B at 50 is specific to inverse-degree. Over all 32 comparisons (4 weightings × 2 graphs × 2 granularities × 2 backends), size-weighted cohesion is lower in all 32, by 0.002–0.019, and beyond the combined seed SD in 23 of them. Hub pull is higher in 21 and lower in 11, which is descriptive only (see Setup).

How I read it:
- On the #919 codebase at about 20 communities, weighting gives a larger largest community and lower modularity: the #919 shape gets worse, not better.
- On the #919 codebase at 40 communities, modularity is slightly higher (+0.010) but the largest community is still larger (about +6).
- On the larger graph at 50 communities it gives a smaller largest community, at a small modularity cost.
- At 100 communities the largest community and hub pull don't move beyond the seed noise, and modularity is slightly higher (+0.007 to +0.009).

A flag whose effect depends this much on the graph and the granularity wouldn't give users a reliable knob, and part of what it does is what `--resolution` already does.

## Why (my reading, not a proof)

- Fortunato & Barthélemy (PNAS 104(1):36–41, 2007) show that modularity optimisation may fail to resolve modules below a scale that depends on the total number of links and on how interconnected the modules are. Berry et al. (Phys. Rev. E 83, 056119, 2011; [arXiv:0903.1072](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.1072)) extend this to weighted graphs, where communities with less than √(Wε/2) total edge weight may go unresolved (W = total edge weight, ε = the heaviest *inter-community* edge). They show that weights derived to keep ε low let small communities be resolved; their title calls it *tolerating* the limit.
- Degree-based weighting doesn't target ε: it lightens *every* edge at a hub, inside the hub's community as much as across it, which fits the mixed result above.
- `structural-triangle` is not Berry et al.'s scheme, just a cheap check that "use local structure instead of degree" isn't an obvious win on these graphs either. 77–81% of their non-loop edges close at least one triangle, so the weight isn't degenerate. It shows the same kind of trade-offs, with no consistent gain.

## `--resolution` and the split passes

[`cluster()`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L279) passes `resolution` to the first partition, but the split passes call [`_split_community(G, nodes)`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L312-L321), which re-partitions with [`_partition(subgraph)`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L344) at the default 1.0. On graph B, `v8` gives *more* communities at 0.25 than at 1.0. With #2388 the count rises with the resolution up to about 4, and 1.0 is unchanged; the numbers, and a side effect on the 25% oversize cap, are on #2388 (https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/2388#issuecomment-5926457601).

## What this does not cover

- Two AST-only code graphs, without semantic or LLM edges, measured on 0.9.71 only.
- My own simple weight formulas, not Berry et al.'s scheme.
- Two granularities per graph for Result 2; hub pull is a descriptive proxy I defined.
- Result 2 is at the partitioner level; Result 1 is at the full `cluster()` level.

## Implications

- I don't think `--edge-weight-mode` is worth adding: on these measurements it has no consistent benefit, and part of its effect overlaps with `--resolution`.
- #2388 is what makes `--resolution` reach the final output, with the side effect on the oversize cap noted there.

Scripts, the two graphs, the patches and the results, with a single `run.sh` that regenerates every number above from public sources: https://gist.github.com/neo1777/9b68c8c24b553af37396781fe1f81da4

Following up on the edge-weight idea above: I measured it on two codebases, and it gives no consistent gain over `--resolution`, so there's no PR for it. Numbers and method: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/919#issuecomment-5926534774.

## Correction to point 3, and a much larger measurement that replaces it

I filed point 3 on a hypothesis I had not verified. I have now measured it and **it is wrong**, so here is the correction plus what the data actually shows. Points 1, 2 and 4 are unaffected.

### What I claimed, and why it was wrong

I wrote that our model "lowercases the path and drops intermediate directories", and asked for a `casefold()` fallback in `_recover_group_path`. I checked that against every built graph we have — 110 `graph.json` files, 21,379 nodes — by taking each node's `source_file` and testing whether it resolves to a real file under that project's source root.

Of the 25 unresolvable examples I sampled, **0 had any uppercase in the basename** and **24 had a basename that does not exist anywhere under the source root**. So a case-insensitive comparison would have recovered none of them. The `casefold()` suggestion is still a cheap hardening, but it is not the fix for this, and I should not have presented it as our failure mode.

### What is actually happening: the model invents paths wholesale

```
nodes with a resolvable source_file :  3,007
nodes with an unresolvable one      : 18,261   (85.4%)
nodes with no source_file at all    :    111
```

The unresolvable values are not corrupted versions of real paths — they are inventions, and several look like the schema's own placeholder shape:

```
diana-rag/insight_1.md   ...   diana-rag/insight_10.md
logs/2024-04-05_15-30-00.log
email_006.txt       invoice_002.txt      payment_confirmation.md
session_01.md       system_alerts.md     project_notes.md
```

Per project, several graphs have **zero** resolvable `source_file` values:

| project (ours) | unresolvable | resolvable |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2,927 | **0** |
| B | 2,540 | 16 |
| C | 1,979 | **0** |
| D | 1,395 | 1,572 |
| E | 1,218 | **0** |

That is the same class as #2217 (model-invented `source_file` bypassing the #1895 filter) — I am adding the magnitude we see on a small local model, since #2217 does not quantify it.

### Why this makes points 1 and 2 worse, not milder

#2973's recovery matches an unresolvable `source_file` by basename against the dispatched allowlist. When the basename is **invented**, there is nothing to match, so the recovery cannot fire however it compares strings — and the group goes to the silent skip. On this backend the recovery path is effectively unreachable.

But the attribution is still recoverable deterministically in the common case, without a model call:

- **A chunk that dispatched exactly one file**: every unresolvable `source_file` in its result can only belong to that file. Assign it.
- **A chunk that dispatched N files**: attribution is genuinely unknown. That is the case that must be *counted and warned*, not dropped in silence — which is the substance of point 1.

A concrete shape, where `_checkpoint_chunk` already has `allowed` in hand:

```python
if len(allowed) == 1:
    only = allowed[0]
    for item in (*nodes, *edges, *hyperedges):
        src = item.get("source_file")
        if src and not source_path(src).is_file():
            item["source_file"] = str(only)     # can only be this file
```

### Revised ask

Replacing point 3 with:

1. Attribute an unresolvable `source_file` to the chunk's only dispatched file when the chunk dispatched one (deterministic, no model call).
2. When attribution is impossible, `warn()` with a count instead of dropping silently — the same gap as point 1.
3. Keep the `casefold()` fallback only as incidental hardening; it is not what our data needed.

One genuinely useful thing I noticed while measuring: when an allowlist *is* passed, 0.9.73 does emit `RuntimeWarning: semantic cache skipped out-of-scope source_file '<path>'; the file was not dispatched for extraction`. That is a real improvement over 0.8.18, which said nothing. The remaining silence is the `if src:` drop in point 1 and the unresolvable-path skip above — neither of which produces any message.

Measured on graphify 0.9.73 and 0.8.18, backend `ollama`, model `qwen2.5:14b` (Q4_K_M), Linux, 110 graphs built from a ~21k-document mostly-Italian-prose corpus.

One more place where the report's `Token cost` line (point 2 of the suggested fix above) comes out wrong. It is in the headless flow and doesn't involve `cost.json`. Checked on 0.9.71 ([`d6eaa8a`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/tree/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a)), and reproduced again on 0.9.73, where these lines are unchanged:

- `graphify extract <path> --backend …` writes the extraction usage into `graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json` as `"tokens"` ([`cli.py#L4615-L4626`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cli.py#L4615-L4626)). It writes no `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and points to `cluster-only` for that.
- `graphify cluster-only` then writes the report with `tokens = label_token_usage` ([`cli.py#L2320`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cli.py#L2320)), which is only its own community-labeling usage (#1694). It also rewrites the sidecar from a dict without `"tokens"` ([`cli.py#L2329-L2339`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cli.py#L2329-L2339)).

So after a paid `extract`:
- the report shows the labeling cost only (`0 input · 0 output` with `--no-label`);
- `"tokens"` is gone from the live `.graphify_analysis.json`. Headless `extract` doesn't write `cost.json` (cf. #1769), so what remains is the dated snapshot that `backup_if_protected` takes before `cluster-only` overwrites anything ([`cli.py#L2285-L2289`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cli.py#L2285-L2289)), and the output-token count in `.graphify_semantic_marker` ([`cli.py#L4599-L4602`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cli.py#L4599-L4602)). Both exist only after an LLM `extract`, so not in the reproducer below.

Reproducer. No LLM is needed: the `python` line stands in for what an LLM `extract` records.

```bash
mkdir t && cd t && printf 'def f():\n    return g()\n\ndef g():\n    return 1\n' > a.py
graphify extract . --code-only
python -c "import json;p='graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json';d=json.load(open(p));d['tokens']={'input':12000,'output':3400};json.dump(d,open(p,'w'))"
graphify cluster-only . --no-label
grep 'Token cost' graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md        # - Token cost: 0 input · 0 output
python -c "import json;print(json.load(open('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json')).get('tokens'))"   # None
```

I tried the obvious fix, carrying `"tokens"` forward in `cluster-only`, and it has a catch that makes it a design call rather than a one-liner. `graphify update` and `extract --no-cluster` rewrite `graph.json` without touching the sidecar. A carried-forward value would then keep reporting an old extraction's cost for a graph that has since changed. The ways out I can see:

- (a) carry it only while the sidecar is not older than `graph.json` (mtime is fragile across filesystems);
- (b) have `extract` store a fingerprint of the graph next to `"tokens"` and check it;
- (c) carry it forward unconditionally, but label the line "cost recorded by the last `extract`", so a stale value isn't presented as this graph's cost.

Whichever option, a `null`/unknown value from #3681 should stay unknown rather than become 0. I haven't opened a PR, since this overlaps #3681; happy to write one for whichever option you prefer.

## Follow-up: we implemented the single-dispatched-file attribution from the correction above, and it recovers the work. Measured on 0.9.73.

Short version: on 0.9.73 the loss is no longer silent — your own warning names it exactly — and the single-file case is recoverable deterministically. Numbers below, in case they are useful for deciding where the fix belongs.

### 0.9.73 already tells you why the work is lost

Running our nightly path on 0.9.73 for the first time, the cache wrote nothing and said:

```
save_semantic_cache: all 10 source_file group(s) were skipped because their paths
do not resolve to real files. This usually means ``root`` is anchored to the wrong
directory (e.g. the --out directory instead of the corpus root). Pass the corpus
directory as ``root`` and the output directory as ``cache_root`` (#1991).
```

Our `root` **is** the corpus root and `cache_root` **is** the output directory — i.e. exactly what the warning advises. The paths do not resolve because the model invented them. So on a weak local backend that warning's suggested cause is a red herring, while the condition it reports is the real and common one. It might be worth softening the wording to mention model mis-attribution as the other cause.

It also surfaced a second failure shape we had not separated from pure invention — a **dropped path segment**:

```
semantic cache skipped out-of-scope source_file 'cantieri-2026-09-01/02-cantiere-fabbrica-cammina.md'
```

where the real path is `cantieri-2026-09-01/02-cantiere-fabbrica-cammina/02-cantiere-fabbrica-cammina.md`. Both shapes occur: fully invented names, and real names with a directory level missing.

### The single-file case is unambiguous, and recovering it is enough to matter

We implemented the rule from the correction above in our own wrapper, by intercepting `save_semantic_cache`: **when `allowed_source_files` contains exactly one path, any `source_file` that does not resolve can only be that file**, so rewrite it. When the allowlist has N entries we touch nothing — attributing at random would write an entry that makes a never-extracted file look done, which is precisely what the #1757 guard exists to prevent.

Measured on the same project, same corpus, same model, cache on (the real incremental path):

| | cache entries written | graph | edges extracted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8.18 (our previous version) | **0** | 58 / 54 | 63 |
| 0.9.73, strict allowlist only | **0** | 58 / 54 | 63 |
| 0.9.73 + single-file attribution | **1** | 57 / 61 | **72** |

The entry that lands: 29 nodes, 31 edges, **31/31 edges carrying `source_file`**, `partial: None`, attributed to the correct file. And the loop closes — a re-read now reports:

```
CACHE: 3 reused, 0 to extract        (was: 2 reused, 1 to extract, every single run)
Extract done in 0.0s: 72n 72e (0 in / 0 out tokens)
```

Before this, that file was re-extracted and discarded on every nightly run. Across our logs that pattern accounted for **394 of 1163 chunks (33.9%)** historically, and **17 of 23 chunks (74%)** on the most recent night.

### Where we think it belongs upstream

`_checkpoint_chunk` already has `allowed = [unit_path(item) for item in chunk]` in hand, so the one-file case is available right there:

```python
if len(allowed) == 1:
    only = allowed[0]
    for item in (*nodes, *edges, *hyperedges):
        src = item.get("source_file")
        if src and not source_path(src).is_file():
            item["source_file"] = str(only)     # can only be this file
```

and for `len(allowed) > 1`, a `warn()` with the count of unattributable groups instead of the silent skip — which is point 1 of the original report.

We are happy to open a PR if that shape is acceptable; say the word and we will match your conventions and add a test for both branches (one-file recovers, N-files warns and does not guess).

Tested this branch merged onto `v8` (e10df08, 0.9.74) on a real Flutter app (~300 Dart files, 6 `part of` files), macOS, Python 3.13, using the normal CLI flow:

```shell
graphify extract . --code-only --force
```

The relative-path case from the test is fixed, but the CLI flow is not affected by this change:

| | nodes with absolute-derived ids |
|---|---|
| `v8` | 202 |
| `v8` + this PR | 202 |

Example: `_AccountRuntime`, declared in `bg_account_runtime.dart` (`part of 'background_service_entry.dart'`), gets the id
`users_<user>_androidstudioprojects_<project>_lib_features_mail_data_background_service_entry_accountruntime`.
The graph itself is consistent (0 dangling edges) - the ids just encode the machine's directory layout.

Why: the CLI hands `extract_dart` absolute paths, so `os.path.normpath(path.parent / parent_ref)` is already absolute and mints the same id as `.resolve()` did. The library's own symbols are then canonicalized by the `prefix_remap` pass in `extract()`, but the part's symbols are skipped, because that pass looks the prefix up by the node's own `source_file`, which is the part, while the prefix belongs to the library. That is point 1 of #3522; this PR addresses point 2 (relative paths).

A minimal sketch that fixed it locally - the extractor records which file the id prefix belongs to, and the remap uses it:

```diff
--- a/graphify/extractors/dart.py
+++ b/graphify/extractors/dart.py
@@ -571,2 +571,6 @@ def extract_dart(path: Path) -> dict:

+    if is_part:
+        for n in nodes:
+            if n.get("source_file"):
+                n["_id_scope_file"] = str(parent_path)
     return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}
--- a/graphify/extract.py
+++ b/graphify/extract.py
@@ -7895,3 +7895,3 @@ def extract(
             try:
-                entry = prefix_remap.get(Path(sf).resolve())
+                entry = prefix_remap.get(Path(n.get("_id_scope_file") or sf).resolve())
             except Exception:
```

Result on the same project: 202 -> 0 absolute-derived ids for Dart (one unrelated `.h` import target remains), still 0 dangling edges, and `_AccountRuntime` becomes `lib_features_mail_data_background_service_entry_accountruntime`. Caveats: as written the hint leaks into `graph.json` and should be dropped after the remap, and I did not check whether the other canonicalization pass (the `#502` one keyed on `source_file`) needs the same hint for incremental `update` runs.

Checked this against current `v8` (0.9.74) and the described vulnerability does not reproduce.

The cited code (`extract.py:2235`, `for src_class_nid in local_classes: new_edges.append(...)`) does not exist anywhere in the current codebase — `_resolve_cross_file_imports` lives in `graphify/extractors/resolution.py`, not `extract.py`, and its current implementation already attributes each `uses` edge only to the specific local symbol whose body actually references the imported name (via a `ref_sources` map built by walking each symbol's own AST subtree), not to every class in the importing file. The docstring even calls this out explicitly: "attribute the `uses` edge to the specific local symbol ... not to every class that merely shares the file (#2652)".

Verified empirically rather than just by reading: built a scaled-down version of the reported shape (one module with 50 classes, 20 importing files each importing all 50 names but each of 8 local classes only referencing one specific imported class in its body). A cartesian-product bug would produce `20 × 8 × 50 = 8000` `uses` edges; the actual run produced exactly `160` (`20 × 8 × 1`), matching the per-reference model, not the cartesian one.

So this looks like a stale finding against pre-#2652 code rather than a live issue on `v8`. No `_MAX_CROSS_FILE_EDGES` cap exists today, but there's also no cartesian multiplier left to cap — edge count stays proportional to actual source references, not `files × imported_names × local_classes`. Happy to revisit if there's a repro that still reproduces the blowup on current `v8`.

I plan to fix this issue.

a finished graphify extract writes with `force=True`. that write skips the shrink check in `to_json`. dedup can then replace `graph.json` with a smaller graph. the command prints no error.

the planned change has three rules.

1. a finished run does not replace `graph.json` when dedup merged nodes and the new node count is lower than the saved count, after nodes from deleted files are subtracted.
2. the command exits with an error. the message shows the old node count, the new node count, and the flag `--allow-dedup-shrink`.
3. `--allow-dedup-shrink` writes that smaller graph. a deleted file still writes. that case does not need the new flag.

`--allow-partial stays` the flag for an incomplete extraction. `--no-dedup` stays the flag that skips dedup.

this change does not change the dedup match rule. that rule is #3094

the test uses two nodes in one file that share a label, plus one node that must remain. dedup still merges that pair after issue 3094. a second test deletes a file and expects the write.

- OpenCode `v2.0.22` (background service, Linux)
- Fresh `graphify install --platform opencode` in a project, then a normal session start

## Fresh log evidence

`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` (`role=server`, run `7caaa3e7`, 2026-10-02):

```
level=WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=/home/maro/Projects/deno/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js
ref=err_04feb898
cause="Cause([Fail(PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id
and an effect or setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at ["default"])))])"

level=WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=.opencode/plugins/graphify.js
ref=err_f6d72e91
cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Could not read package.json: Error: ENOENT:
no such file or directory, open '/home/maro/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js/package.json'))])"
```

Additional detail vs. the original report: the bare relative spec resolved against **`$HOME`**, not the project directory (project is `/home/maro/Projects/deno`, but the ENOENT path is `/home/maro/.opencode/...`). Worth checking the resolution base for the `plugin` key as well as the key name itself.

While the `plugin` key was present, we also saw repeated:

```
level=WARN message="failed to check plugin update" target=.opencode/plugins/graphify.js
cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Package checks only support registry and Git package specs)))"
```

## Fix verification

Applied exactly the suggested fix from this issue:

1. Rewrote the emitted file as a plain-object V2 default export (`{ id: "graphify", async setup(ctx) }`), registering the hook via `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)`, accepting both `shell` and `bash` tool ids, mutating `event.input.command`.
2. Removed the `plugin` key from `.opencode/opencode.json` (auto-discovery handles `.opencode/plugins/`).

After `opencode service restart`:

- `INFO msg="loading plugin" id=/home/maro/Projects/deno/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` with **no failure following it**
- zero `failed to load plugin` / `failed to check plugin update` entries in the new run
- the reminder hook verifiably fires (the `[graphify] knowledge graph at graphify-out/...` echo was prepended to the first shell command of the session, visible in the log's spawn line)

**Conclusion:** the reference port in this issue works as-is; it just needs to land in `graphify/install.py::_OPENCODE_PLUGIN_JS`, and `_install_opencode_plugin` should drop the `plugin`-key registration. Note that any local patch is necessarily temporary — the next `graphify install` overwrites it, so the upstream emit is the only durable fix.

This issue describes a case I can reproduce consistently, and which still reproduces on the latest published release. Posting the minimal repro in case it is useful for validating the fix.

## Minimal reproduction

Fixture (2 files):

```
package/
  __init__.py    0 bytes
  views.py       9 lines
```

`views.py`:

```python
from typing import Any
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser


def detail(request: Any, user: AbstractUser) -> Any:
    return user
```

Both referenced types are **defined outside the scanned corpus**:
`typing.Any` and `django.contrib.auth.models.AbstractUser`.

Command:

```bash
graphify extract ./fixture --out ./out --code-only
```

## Result

The type references are emitted as `code` nodes with no provenance at all:

```
id=abstractuser   file_type=code  _origin=ast  source_file=""  source_location=""
id=any            file_type=code  _origin=ast  source_file=""  source_location=""
```

Empty `source_file`, empty `source_location`, and no `origin_file` either — there is no anchor left to resolve.

The interesting part is visible in the same graph. The **modules** are recorded correctly as external concepts:

```
id=typing                     file_type=concept  type=external
id=django_contrib_auth_models  file_type=concept  type=external
```

So the module is classified as an external reference, while the type it exposes is emitted as an orphan `code` node. That is the inconsistency described in this issue: the type reference is neither rewired to a canonical definition nor classified as an external reference.

## Versions tested

| version | `source_file=""` type nodes |
|---|---|
| `graphifyy 0.9.72` | 2 |
| `graphifyy 0.9.74` | 2 |

The two runs produce identical nodes (same ids, same order, same fields). **0.9.74, the latest published release, does not fix this.**

## Wider observation

The same signature is not isolated to this fixture. In a Python codebase I scanned, the identical shape (`file_type=code`, `_origin=ast`, no `source_file`, no `source_location`) appears repeatedly, with node ids matching the bare lowercased type names (`abstractuser`, `any`, etc.). The count scales with the number of cross-module type references, which is consistent with this being a systematic extraction issue rather than a one-off.

No proprietary data is included here; the fixture is synthetic and the larger observation is described only as a pattern.

## Relation to #3254

PR #3254 appears related to the broader sourceless-type-stub family, but this external-definition case was not tested against that PR, so I cannot say whether it would be covered.

## Environment

```text
graphify 0.9.72 / 0.9.74
Python 3.13
Windows
```

The tension is that this key is what catches the LLM/AST ghost twins. A fix that keeps same-file nodes with different `source_location` would also let some real ghosts through, unless the location is part of the key or the collapse is limited to nodes with no location.

Thanks for the review. Here's where the four findings ended up:

1. **Grok hook matchers (install.py):** I've kept Claude's names on purpose. Grok's hook matcher looks up each term of a plain `|` list in its Claude alias table, so `Bash|Grep` already matches `run_terminal_command`, `grep` and `hashline_grep`, and `Read|Glob` matches `read_file`, `hashline_read` and `list_dir`. That's in grok-build's `xai-grok-hooks/src/matcher.rs` (`exact_names`, with tests such as `claude_bash_matches_grok_tool`) and `xai-grok-tools/src/types/claude_alias.rs`. Using the same entries as Claude also lets Grok merge them with the same graphify hook when it imports `.claude/settings.json`, so the hook runs once instead of twice. e6e107c had switched to Grok-only names; 957acd6 puts the Claude entries back and adds these source links to the `_install_grok_hook` docstring.
2. **All-cached run skipping `.graphify_semantic.json`:** Fixed for Grok in the sequential skillgen fragment (e6e107c, tightened in 957acd6). When everything is cached, the skill now skips B1/B2 but still runs B3, so `.graphify_semantic.json` exists before Part C. The other hosts' skills on v8 have the same "skip to Part C directly" text. I haven't changed those here.
3. **Step 2 splicing INPUT_PATH:** This comes from the shared skillgen core, and every v8 skill has the same line (`detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))`), so it isn't something this PR introduced. e6e107c had changed the shared core, which also changed the generated skills for about 15 other hosts. To keep this PR focused on Grok, 957acd6 reverts that, and every non-Grok skill is back to the v8 output. I'm happy to send the `.graphify_root` change as a separate PR for all hosts.
4. **Chunk merge aborting on invalid JSON:** The merge loop is also shared core text and is the same on v8. For Grok, the sequential B3 step now tells the agent to rename an invalid chunk to `.graphify_chunk_NN.json.invalid` before merging. The merge only reads `*.json` files, so it skips that chunk. The shared merge loop is unchanged (reverted in 957acd6), and hardening it for every host can go in the same follow-up as point 3.

The coupling notes are fan-out metrics on the existing install dispatchers and `_render_core`. The new Grok branches follow the existing Codex/amp ones, so I didn't refactor them here.

I ran the live-model check I'd listed under Limitations, using Grok Build 1.0.46 (grok-4.7, signed in with a grok.com account, no API key). I ran headless `grok --always-approve -p` in a trusted throwaway repo, after `graphify grok install --project` and `graphify update .`, with a raw-stdin logging hook next to graphify's. I used three short prompts:
- read `auth.py` and explain `login`
- run `grep -r password . --include=*.py`
- the read prompt again, with `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1 GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT_TTL=0`

What I saw:
- **Matchers:** `Bash|Grep` and `Read|Glob` fired for `run_terminal_command`, `grep`, `read_file` and `list_dir` through Grok's alias matching.
- **Payloads:** they carry both snake_case and camelCase keys (`tool_name`/`toolName`, `tool_input`/`toolInput`, `session_id`/`sessionId`, …). The tool inputs are `command` (run_terminal_command), `pattern`/`glob` (grep), `target_file` (read_file) and `target_directory` (list_dir).
- **Search nudge:** it reached the model as a system reminder, and the model ran `graphify query` next.
- **Bug found:** `read_file` sends `target_file`, not `path` as I had assumed. So on 957acd6 the read guard said nothing on every Grok read: no nudge and no strict deny. Fixed in 4f42a10, with tests built from the captured payload.
- **After the fix:** the read nudge reached the model. In strict mode, the first `read_file` (sent in parallel with `graphify query`) was denied once ("Hook denied: graphify strict mode: …"), and the re-sent read went through with the nudge.

On 4f42a10, the full suite passes on 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 (all extras). ruff is clean, pyright shows no new errors compared with v8, and the five skillgen checks pass. Update: I also ran `/graphify .` live on 4f42a10 on a sample repo with code and a markdown doc. It built `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `graph.html`, and a cached rerun still wrote `.graphify_semantic.json` and rebuilt the same graph (80 nodes, 127 edges). Not exercised live: Windows/PowerShell and the `hashline_*` tools.

Hey, I'd like to take this one. I reproduced it on 0.9.75 with jvzelst-tech's script (3 files in, 1 out), so it's still happening after #4014.

I have a fix working locally, but it has one tradeoff I'd like your OK on. Right now, nothing tells a repeated heading like `Decisions` apart from a real entity like a person's name, because both are unstamped `document` nodes. So my fix makes dedup merge `document`/`rationale` nodes across files only when they're stamped `node_kind: "entity"`. The extraction prompts (skill and `llm.py`) now ask for `node_kind` (`heading`/`entity`), so #296's cross-file merging keeps working for new extractions.

The catch is that graphs extracted before this won't merge entities across files until they're re-extracted, and two #296 tests need the `entity` stamp added. The reporter's case passes, and the full suite has no new failures. This is separate from #4019, which is about merges within one file.

on the page node as `frontmatter` (`extractors/markdown.py:408-413`), but `_node_search_text` never reads it

return "No matching nodes found", while the same call finds label terms. With #3636 as written this stays true,
because the markdown extractor writes no `body` attribute.

Request, either of:

1. Have `extract_markdown` also emit a capped `body` from the frontmatter `description`/`summary` (and optionally the
   first paragraph).
2. Let the #3636 tier read string values of `frontmatter` at the same lower weight.

Option 1 keeps the single documented convention (`body`) that #3636 chose. Happy to provide a fixture.

This is a significant bug. When Gemini silently omits files in an oversized chunk, the knowledge graph becomes incomplete without any warning, leading to incorrect query results.

**Root cause hypothesis:**
The chunking logic likely has a token_budget check that skips files exceeding the threshold, but doesn't log or warn about the omission. The 60K default may be too conservative for Gemini's actual context window.

**Suggested fixes:**
1. **Log omitted files**: When a file exceeds token_budget, log a warning with file path and size
2. **Auto-split large files**: Instead of omitting, split large files into multiple chunks that fit within budget
3. **Configurable budget**: Allow users to set token_budget per provider/model
4. **Validation step**: After chunking, verify total files processed vs total files in repo

**Quick diagnostic:**
Can you check if the omitted files appear in the chunking logs with a 'skipped' or 'omitted' status? That would confirm the silent drop behavior.

Validated this live with gemini-3-flash-preview on a synthetic 30-doc corpus (about 65K tokens, mirroring the reported setup), running the exact arms from the issue with --max-concurrency 1.

Results: could not reproduce the 24/30 omission. The forced single-chunk arm covered 30/30 files on uniform docs (25 percent out:in ratio) and 29/29 dispatched files on a diverse mixed md/yml set (6 percent ratio). So the collapse does not appear deterministic on chunk size alone. It likely depends on dense entity-rich docs, or the preview model has shifted since the report.

Two observations in support of the proposed fixes. First, the diverse single-chunk run landed at 6 percent output ratio, squarely in the reported sick band, presenting as thin coverage (about 1 node per file) rather than dropped files, so the ratio signal looks real. Second, from code the retry concern checks out: omission without truncation re-sends the identical chunk, which cannot succeed on its own.

Supporting the proposed changes (explicit short-but-valid message plus capped retries on non-truncated omissions) even without a full repro. Happy to re-run against the original corpus if it can be shared.

@brlumen thank you for testing on a real project and for the diagnosis. You were right: the CLI flow hands `extract()` absolute paths, so the part's symbols still got the library's absolute-derived prefix. The prefix remap then looked them up by their `source_file`, which is the part.

I took your approach in 6a280f6 and closed the two gaps you mentioned:

- `extract_dart` stamps the library on a part's symbol nodes as `_id_scope_file`. The part's own file node is not stamped; its id is already the part's.
- `extract()` looks the prefix up through `_id_scope_file` when it is set. It also registers that file the way it registers `target_file` edge targets, so the library's prefixes are known when only the part is in the batch. That is the incremental `update` case. Without the registration, re-extracting the part on its own kept the absolute ids.
- The stamp is popped next to `local_alias` before output, so it does not reach `graph.json`.

The new `test_part_of_ids_are_canonical_through_extract_with_absolute_paths` runs `extract()` on absolute paths twice: once with the library and the part, once with the part alone. Both times it asserts that `DeriveHelper` is `lib_core_settlement_settlement_derivehelper`, that no node or edge id contains the scan root, and that no node keeps `_id_scope_file`. It fails on the previous head. Five single mutants fail the Dart tests: no registration, a lookup that ignores the stamp, a stamp that is never dropped, a stamp that is never set, and resolving the parent again.

I also merged `v8`. Its new `test_part_file_keeps_its_own_node` expected the library id from the resolved path, which is the behaviour this PR changes, so it now expects the id the library's own extraction mints. The full suite gives the same 61 failures on `v8` and on this branch; they come from optional grammars missing in my env, such as `tree_sitter_erlang`. Passes are 6115 on `v8` and 6117 here.

@andrebrait thanks for running this downstream and for the follow-up. All three gaps are real, and your commit is now on this branch with your authorship kept (093421d), on top of a merge of current `v8`. The merge adds `v8`'s `_nudge_for_out` wrapper to each nudge your commit budgets: the search nudge, the read nudge and the stale notice. `tests/test_hook_guard.py` and `tests/test_hook_strict.py` pass (112), and the full suite shows the same environment-only failures as `v8` (optional grammars I don't have installed) with 12 more passes. So #3893 can be closed if you agree; it carries the same two commits.

- A re-run without --force re-sends only the missing files. With a doc-heavy corpus, though, those still fit in a single 60K chunk, so the same omission is likely to happen again.
- The README has no troubleshooting entry for "N files produced no nodes, 0 truncated or hollow". The output-token explanation is under the invalid-JSON entry.

I'd split this into two PRs:

1. Diagnostics (small). When files are missing and nothing was truncated or hollow, say so directly: "the model returned a short but valid response; N files were not addressed". Suggest a smaller --token-budget, and add a README troubleshooting entry. I'll build on #3617 so we don't conflict.
2. Retry (follow-up). Inside the same run, re-send only the missing files in smaller sub-chunks, limited by the existing retry depth (no retries when the depth is 0). This adds cost, so I'd like your OK on the approach before I write it.

I'm leaving the default token_budget unchanged, since it affects every user and the omission hasn't been reproduced consistently. Happy to change that if you'd rather lower it.

A couple of things that speed up review: make sure the test suite passes on Python 3.10 and 3.13, and that the change keeps extraction deterministic.

### Confirmed and reproduced.

### Root Cause
1. **Flat default manifest**: `_MANIFEST_PATH` in `graphify/detect.py` defaults to `graphify-out/manifest.json`. When graphing subfolder B (`experts/`) followed by an incremental scan on subfolder A (`workflows/`), subfolder B's manifest is loaded and re-anchored to subfolder A (`workflows/expert.py`), which does not exist and gets reported as deleted.
2. **Double-nesting on workspace manifests**: Running an incremental scan on a subfolder against a workspace manifest joins workspace-relative keys (`workflows/workflow.py`) with the subfolder root, resulting in invalid doubled paths (`workflows/workflows/workflow.py`).
3. **Missing root boundary filter**: `detect_incremental()` iterates through all loaded manifest rows without verifying whether each path actually falls within `root`.

### Fix
1. Scope default manifest paths per scan root via `manifest_path_for_root(root)` (`graphify-out/<slug>/manifest.json`) when `root` is a subfolder, while preserving `graphify-out/manifest.json` for repo-level runs and falling back to the workspace manifest if no subfolder manifest exists yet.
2. In `_to_absolute_from_storage()`, walk parent directories if `root / key` does not exist on disk to resolve ancestor/workspace-relative keys without duplicating paths.
3. In `detect_incremental()`, skip entries outside `root` (`if not _in_root(f): continue`) so foreign paths are neither reported as deletions nor exclusions.

I investigated the missing call edges in Express and other CommonJS codebases.

#### Rca
In Express, methods are attached to module objects before being exported (`res.format = function(obj) { ... }; module.exports = res`). 

In `graphify/extractors/engine.py`:
1. `_js_extra_walk` only captured `exports.x = fn` and `<Class>.prototype.x = fn`. It intentionally ignored arbitrary `obj.x = fn` to prevent phantom god-nodes (#1077).
2. Because `res.format` was not recognized as a method node, its AST body was never appended to `function_bodies`.
3. `walk_calls` never walked the body of `res.format`, meaning calls made inside it (such as `normalizeType(...)`) were never emitted or resolved to their imported functions.

#### Solution
1. Added `_js_find_exported_objects()` to identify top-level identifiers exported via CommonJS/ESM (`module.exports = res`, `exports = module.exports = res`, `module.exports = { res }`, etc.).
2. In `_js_extra_walk`, when a member function is assigned to an exported object (`owner_name in exported_names`), we emit the method node and append its body to `function_bodies` so `walk_calls` extracts its internal call sites.
3. Arbitrary unexported objects (`const obj = {}; obj.whatever = () => 1;`) remain ignored, preserving the #1077 guard.

The `to_json` difference is the guard, with one real hole in it.

Nodes `1`, `2`, and `3` have no `_origin` and no `L` location, so they count as semantic. A second save of that same graph returned false because the check only treated a string id as present. Integer `1` was already in the new graph. `93c43cf` looks up the id first, and only then applies the string remap. A missing integer id still refuses: saved `4`, new graph `{1, 2, 3}`.

`to_json` still passes an empty deleted set. That function has no list of files the user removed. `graphify update` passes `deleted_paths` into `_check_shrink`, and that is the path that may drop a semantic node on a deleted file. I am not inventing a deleted set inside `to_json`.

The coupling note and the findings outside this diff are functions this change does not edit. Leaving those.

### Update Addressing Bot Review & Verification

1. Pure Lexical Resolution in \_to_absolute_from_storage\: Reverted all filesystem calls (\.exists()\) and ancestor traversal in \_to_absolute_from_storage\. The function remains strictly a lexical path normalizer that never touches disk, eliminating the formal verification discrepancy and ensuring no deletion can ever be masked by ancestor files.
2. Fixed CLI \--out\ Manifest Locations: Removed slug directory redirects on default manifest paths so explicit \--out\ CLI options and default output directories are never moved.
3. Anchor Resolution via \_manifest_storage_anchor\: Handled subfolder manifest re-anchoring by inspecting whether \
oot\ is a subfolder of the manifest's containing workspace root (\manifest_path.parent.parent\), correctly resolving relative paths without double-nesting.
4. Out-of-Root Containment Filter: Manifest entries outside \
oot\ continue to be skipped cleanly in \detect_incremental\.

On the advisory about escaped `customConditions`: that is the intended fail-closed path. The shared JSONC reader can rewrite string contents (its trailing-comma pass turns `"custom,}"` into `"custom}"`), so the fallback only trusts a condition that appears verbatim as a JSON string literal in the config that sets it. A condition written with escapes, such as `"@zod\/source"`, doesn't match that check, the fallback is skipped, and the import keeps exactly its v8 result. It's listed under the refusals in the description. If you'd rather accept escaped forms, the cleaner fix is a string-aware trailing-comma pass in `_strip_jsonc`, which I left out of this PR because it changes the shared reader for every config.

The coupling notes are on `_load_tsconfig_custom_conditions`, which merges the `extends` chain and applies the refusals, and on `_resolve_workspace_import`, which now calls the fallback after the unchanged v8 walk.

**Direct answer to @nothariharan's question:** the omitted files do **not** get a `skipped`/`omitted` status anywhere in the chunking log. There is no per-file marker at chunk time. - **Both `WARNING` lines cap at 5 names + `(+N more)`.** Everything above came from `graphify-out/.graphify_incremental.json` (`files.document`) intersected with the written graph, not from the log.

Follow-up with a **third arm** — this refines the "chunk size vs model" question.

I re-ran the same Scripts corpus through a different model at the **default `token_budget=60000`**. Result: the oversized single chunk is **not** what breaks it — the model is.

| backend / model        | `--token-budget` | chunks | docs omitted | input tok | output tok | ratio     | nodes   |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------ | ------------ | --------- | ---------- | --------- | ------- |
| gemini-3-flash-preview | 60000            | 1      | **24 / 30**  | 59,989    | 1,899      | 3.2%      | 901     |
| gemini-3-flash-preview | 15000            | 4      | 3 / 30       | 62,425    | 9,068      | 14.5%     | 931     |
| **deepseek-v4-flash**  | **60000**        | **1**  | **0 / 30**   | 56,439    | 16,423     | **29.1%** | **945** |

`deepseek-v4-flash` covered **all 30 files in a single ~56K-token chunk** — no `produced no nodes` warning was emitted, and I verified 30/30 present by diffing the dispatch list against `source_file` in the written `graph.json`. Every one of the 24 files gemini omitted at the same budget is present here.

So the collapse is **model-specific coverage behavior on a large multi-file chunk**, not a deterministic property of the chunk size. That is consistent with @nothariharan's finding that it isn't deterministic on chunk size alone, and with `gpt-oss:120b-cloud` not collapsing — but now with a clean same-30-doc, same-default-budget comparison instead of a smaller payload.

- **It's not a stock graphify backend.** The endpoint is OpenCode Go (`https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`), registered as a custom provider in `~/.graphify/providers.json`; it needs an `x-opencode-session` header that graphify can't currently set natively (worked around via `OPENAI_CUSTOM_HEADERS`; filed as #3680). - **Not a byte-identical replay.** The gemini arms were graphify 0.9.75; this arm is 0.9.77, and the repo scanned as 217 code / 30 docs vs 213 code / 30 docs in October. @belentani7 — I tested that one directly, and I think "60K is too conservative for Gemini's context window" is the direction that doesn't apply here. Raising it changes nothing:

| `--token-budget` | chunks | docs omitted | input  | output |
| ---------------- | ------ | ------------ | ------ | ------ |
| 60000            | 1      | 24 / 30      | 60,799 | 1,873  |
| **150000**       | **1**  | **24 / 30**  | 60,799 | 1,873  |

The whole 30-doc corpus is ~60K input tokens, so it already packs into a single chunk at the default — i.e. at 60K the packer is cramming all 30 small files into one request. `token_budget` is a chunk-packing cap, not a context-window cap, so raising it can't go below one chunk, and the single chunk is exactly the failing shape. Gemini's context is ~1M, so context was never the limit (graphify also reports 0 truncated).

The direction that works is the opposite: `--token-budget 15000` → 4 chunks → 2/30 omitted.

I also checked the thinking budget (`reasoning_effort` is hardcoded `low` for gemini): forcing high moved 24→17 omitted, still collapsing. Max-output was never binding (cap 16,384, used 1,873). So the deficit isn't budget/context in any of the three senses — it's the model's coverage over one oversized multi-file chunk. The rest of your list (log omitted files, per-provider budget, post-chunk validation) is exactly on target.

Third validation arm from my side, dense entity-rich corpus this time (30 runbooks, about 72K input tokens in one chunk, the closest I could get to your setup synthetically): 30/30 files covered, 30 nodes, 72,619 in / 2,814 out (3.9%). Same picture as before. Thin output in the sick band, zero omission. Three corpora, zero reproductions of the 24/30 drop, which supports the refined conclusion that the chunk is necessary but not sufficient.

One code-level confirmation for the diagnostics scope: your logging claim checks out exactly. The warning caps at 5 names (llm.py), while the full uncovered_files list is built in the same function but lives only in memory and is consumed for the shrink guard (cli.py), never persisted. So post-run the full omitted set is unrecoverable except by the dispatch-vs-graph diff you described. Dumping that list to a file is a precise small win and I would put it first in the diagnostics PR.

Thanks @nikhilsaxena04, and nice investigation on the Windows hang. Closing this one because the fix targets the wrong code path: issue #3646's faulthandler stack pins the hang inside `tempfile.mkstemp()` at `paths.py:120` (CPython retrying up to TMP_MAX when the output dir is held by AV/indexer), but this PR wraps `os.replace`/`os.rename`, which run *after* mkstemp returns — so the reported scenario never reaches the changed lines. There's also no lock in `paths.py`, so it's a mkstemp retry stall rather than a concurrency deadlock. The retry logic itself is well-formed; if you move a bounded retry (ideally plus an actionable error surfacing the target path) to the mkstemp call at `paths.py:120` and add a test that patches `mkstemp`/`os.open` to reproduce the spin, we'd be glad to take it.

Thanks @nikhilsaxena04 — the direction here is good and it's deterministic (no #1667 exposure); the sub-phrase bonus and evidence-first truncation are sound. Two blockers before it can land:

1. **Restore the parity test.** The PR adds `if not seeded_with_same_label and len(ref_seeds) == 3: continue` to `test_pick_seeds_with_optimized_best_seed_matches_legacy_semantics`, which silently skips the per-term assertion for the 3-seed case. That test's graph sets no `community` attribute, so the new filter is provably a no-op there and the test should pass unmodified — the skip masks a possible regression and contradicts the PR's own 'legacy parity' claim. Please remove it and let the test pass as-is.
2. **Don't drop the top-scored seed.** The community-coherence filter can discard the single highest-scoring seed when it's a community minority (your own test asserts a score-10.0 node being dropped). Add a guard that always retains seed #1, and test against real community-detection output rather than hand-set community ints.

Non-blocking but worth doing given this targets large graphs: the evidence `nx.shortest_path` runs over the full graph per seed-pair on every render — operate on the induced `G.subgraph(nodes)` instead. Also, splitting the three heuristics into separate PRs would make each easier to evaluate and land. Happy to re-review once 1 and 2 are addressed.

Thanks @bastiennoel93 — the root-cause fix is correct and minimal: `export default '<long base64>'` was being treated as a module specifier and resolved against `baseUrl`, so `candidate.is_file()` threw ENAMETOOLONG and aborted the whole rebuild. Stopping the string-child fallback for `export_statement` is the right call, and genuine `from` re-exports aren't affected.

One blocker: a crash fix needs a regression test. Please add the #4166 repro (a tsconfig with `baseUrl: "."` plus `export default '<long base64>'`) asserting extraction doesn't crash and no `ref_data_image`-style import edge is minted. Strongly recommended alongside it: wrap the `candidate.is_file()` / `resolved_path.is_file()` calls in `try/except OSError` (the codebase already does this at `extract.py:790-791` and `815-819`) so any *other* over-length derived string skips one file instead of aborting the whole rebuild — that's the defense-in-depth the issue asked for. Add the test and we can land it.

On the bot's point (target missing when the entry is written, created later): I checked it. `user.py` imports a module that doesn't exist yet, build, create the module, then warm update vs cold build of the same tree:

- Python (`from pkg.slice import cut`): warm == cold, on v8 and with this PR. The missing-module id (`pkg_slice`) is the same id the file gets once it exists, so the replayed edge already lands on the real node.
- JS (`import { cut } from './slice.js'`): JS is in `_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`, so there is no hit to replay. Edges are equal; the one extra node on the warm side is an edgeless `ref_slice_js` stub stamped `semantic`, which is #4180 and is gone with #4181 applied (then warm == cold fully).

So that case behaves exactly as on v8 here, and I kept it out of scope (it's in the limitations line).

Rebased onto `v8` 0.9.80 (6478eb7) to clear the new conflict in `engine.py`.

The conflict was the #3797 cast receiver (`((IStore)x).M()` / `(x as IStore).M()`), which `v8` added as one more inline arm in the invocation branch that this PR replaces with `_csharp_member_receiver`. I moved that arm into the helper rather than keeping a second copy, so the call site behaves exactly as it does on `v8`: both #3797 cast tests in `test_csharp_member_calls.py` pass, and fail if the arm is removed from the helper. Because the helper is shared, a property read through a cast now resolves on the cast type too. One new test covers that (`test_cast_receiver_binds_to_the_cast_types_property`).

Real-run evidence for the bot's first advisory finding ("Coverage verifier treats files with missing coverage entries as complete"). In my case it wasn't hypothetical, and the file was never opened at all, not just partly read.

Skill-path `--update` on 0.9.69 (the extraction prompt and B1 are unchanged in 0.9.80): 15 docs (~660 KB) in 3 chunks by file count.
- **Chunk of 12 files (~200 KB):** the subagent read 40-60 lines of 8 files and **never opened the other 4**. It still emitted nodes and edges for those 4 from their file names alone, marked `INFERRED` (19 nodes). The chunk was well-formed JSON.
- **Chunk of 2 files (~197 KB):** it used only the headings of a 143 KB HTML file and the first 250 lines of a 54 KB doc. Those two files are 970 and 894 lines, 1,864 combined, so this chunk passes both the 2000-line solo rule and the ~6000-line cap. Only a byte bound would have split it.

Both were caught only because the subagents admitted it in their replies.

Two suggestions from that:
1. **In B3.5, treat a FILE_LIST entry with no coverage entry as unread,** not complete. Re-queue it, and don't keep nodes whose `source_file` has no reported coverage. A subagent that invents nodes for a file won't report coverage for it, so "missing" is exactly the failure signature.
2. **Widen the prompt rule from partly-read to never-read files:** "Never derive a node or an edge from a file name, a path, or content you have not read. INFERRED means inferred from text you read, not guessed from a title."

I've been running a local patch along these lines (an `unread_files` list, a byte cap per chunk, and re-dispatch of anything unread). I can share it if useful, but your coverage map is the better vehicle.

Fixed in PR #4239.

What changed:
- `graphify/cache.py`: the AST cache directory is now `cache/ast/v{graphifyy_version}-s{schema}-g{grammar_fingerprint}/`.
- `_grammar_fingerprint()` hashes the installed `tree-sitter` runtime plus every `tree-sitter-*` distribution's exact version (incl. `tree-sitter-language-pack`), memoized once per process.
- Upgrading any grammar package therefore moves `extract()` to a new cache dir; the existing stale-dir sweep removes the old one, so stale post-upgrade results are never served and no manual cache clear is needed.

Verified with new regression tests in `tests/test_grammar_cache_key.py` (fingerprint changes on grammar bump, stable for unchanged set, cache dir changes end-to-end). `ruff check` clean; reviewed by an agent for bypasses/test gaps (fixed: per-dist error isolation, non-vacuous stability test, end-to-end dir-change test).

- Keep transitive minimums in one `tool.uv.constraint-dependencies` list and use `uv sync --locked` in Docker, rather than maintaining a second handwritten pip constraints file. UV is digest-pinned, and a stale manifest/lock fails installation.
- Preserve the existing base Python/pip pairing, non-root UID and HTTP entrypoint. The container uses the single-project `/usr/local` prefix with `--inexact` to retain base-image tools; this is not a claim that OS packages or pip's vendored libraries are remediated.
- Selectively update the lock, preserving unrelated pins and NumPy/Python compatibility markers. The policy also covers fsspec, PyJWT 2.15 and soupsieve 2.9, alongside the virtualenv floor already in this PR.
- Add a real offline UV resolver regression: a synthetic vulnerable wheel is admitted without the policy and rejected with it, without installing the old library. Add RSA/JWT interoperability and expired-claims/options-reuse regression checks, plus an offline native CLI extraction/query fixture.
- Include a short design/spec explaining the single policy owner and limitations. UV constraints are not wheel `Requires-Dist` metadata; unconstrained PyPI/pip installation is outside this guarantee.

Fixed in #4275 — and here's exactly what was wrong, how it's fixed, and what's deliberately left out.

## Why #114 didn't cover this

#114 replaced **one** block — the inline `save_query_result` Python — with `graphify save-result` (v0.3.18), then closed. Every other pipeline step and every on-demand reference flow kept its inline Python. biggates' follow-up comment in #114 flagged exactly that ("there are still a lot of other raw python scripts in skills… are you going to do all of them?"), but it was never turned into work — which is what this issue tracks.

## Root cause

Each step ran as:

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
# ... 10-20 lines of Python with # comments
"
```

Two Claude Code heuristics fire on that, once per step, and neither is allowlistable: `command_substitution` (the `$(cat …)`) and "newline followed by `#` in a quoted argument" (the Python comments). ~30 manual approvals per run.

## How it's fixed

Every step is now a plain console command. The step bodies moved into a new `graphify/pipeline.py` and are exposed as `graphify pipeline <step>` — `detect`, `extract-ast`, `empty-semantic`, `cache-check`, `merge-chunks`, `save-cache`, `merge-semantic`, `merge-extraction`, `build`, `diagnose`, `label`, `save-manifest`, `cleanup`, plus `vocab`, `transcribe`, `detect-incremental`, `code-only-check`, `empty-extract`, `update-merge`, `graph-diff` for the reference flows. The references now call those plus existing commands (`graphify query/path/explain/save-result/add/watch`) and the `graphify-mcp` console script.

Result: no `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)`, no inline `python -c`, and `Bash(graphify *)` is now allowlistable — so the ~30 prompts per run are gone and the injection surface shrinks (arguments go through argparse instead of string interpolation).

The skill is generated from `tools/skillgen/fragments/`; the edits are in the fragments and all generated artifacts were regenerated + blessed, so nothing drifts.

## Verified

- Old vs new produce **byte-identical** `.graphify_*` sidecars, `graph.json`, `manifest.json`, and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` on a real corpus — same graph, different delivery.
- Full test suite: **no new failures** vs the pre-change baseline.
- New tests cover the pipeline steps end to end (including the incremental `--update` flow and the `#479` shrink guard) and a drift guard that fails if any split host or reference reintroduces an inline `-c` block.
- Reviewed twice by a separate agent; all findings fixed.

## What's intentionally not in this PR

`skill-aider.md` and `skill-devin.md` still contain inline Python (37 and 39 blocks). That's **not Claude Code** — those are the Aider and Devin hosts, which #197 doesn't report. They're also a genuinely wide change: unlike the split hosts, they aren't generated from `core.md` + references — each is a hand-maintained ~1,300–1,400-line monolith that inlines everything, and they're **frozen against a pinned v8 blob** by `monolith_roundtrip`, which requires every changed line to match a sanctioned-diff predicate. Converting them means rewriting 76 blocks *and* adding a new sanctioned-diff predicate and re-validating the round-trip. That's a clean follow-up PR on its own; folding it in would have ballooned the blast radius of this one.

So: **#197 (Claude Code) is fully resolved**; the aider/devin monoliths are the one tracked follow-up. Step 1's one-time interpreter *detection* still uses `$(…)` — that's inherent to installing/detecting graphify, and it's a single block, not per-step.

Rebased onto `v8` 0.9.84 (2cb81c6) to clear the new `engine.py` conflict.

This time the conflict was #4246's chained receivers in the invocation branch: `x.F.M()`, typed through `x`'s field `F`, and `xs[i].M()`, typed as the element type. Both feed `csharp_receiver_chain` from the method's receiver table, which only the call site has, so they stay inline at the call site. `_csharp_member_receiver` still handles the simple receivers (identifier / `this` / `base` / `this.field` / cast), and the chain arms run only when it returns nothing. That is the same order `v8`'s if/elif chain uses, so calls resolve exactly as on `v8`. `tests/test_csharp_member_chain_calls.py` passes, and 5 of its tests fail if the chain fallback is disabled.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_csharp*.py tests/test_cross_language_call_resolution.py   229 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q   (two halves)
  2cb81c6 (v8):  12 failed, 6814 passed, 222 skipped
  this branch:   12 failed, 6835 passed, 222 skipped
  (the failing set is identical and none are C# tests; the +21 are this PR's tests)
uv run ruff check .                                     All checks passed!
python -m tools.skillgen --check / --audit-coverage / --schema-singleton /
  --monolith-roundtrip / --always-on-roundtrip           all ok
```

Thanks for picking this up so quickly. I ran an A/B test of this PR on the repository where I hit the warnings. It removes the warnings, but the restored nodes come back with **no edges**, so in practice little changes compared to before.

**Setup**

- Corpus: a mixed repo (MicroPython firmware, an HTML page, Markdown docs), ~1,500 nodes, 39 semantic files. Paths and IDs below are shortened, as in the issue.
- `extract --backend claude-cli --token-budget 4500`, then `cluster-only`.
- Both runs replayed the same semantic cache (39 hit / 0 miss, 0 re-extracted), so the extraction output was identical between runs.
- **Baseline:** `2cb81c6` (this PR's parent, identical to the 0.9.84 release). **PR:** `ddf0460b`. Each was installed in its own venv and started from the same `graphify-out/cache`.
- For reference I also compared against my committed graph from 0.9.83. That comparison includes the 0.9.83→0.9.84 changes; the baseline-vs-PR pair is the clean comparison.

**Results**

| | "minted by two different files" warnings | nodes | edges |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9.83 (committed graph) | n/a | 1524 | 2558 |
| baseline `2cb81c6` (0.9.84) | 2 | 1523 | 2558 |
| PR `ddf0460b` | 0 | 1525 | 2558 |

The only differences between baseline and PR are the two new nodes. The edge set is identical, no existing ID, label or `source_file` changed, and there are no new warnings or dangling edges.

**Problem 1: edges don't follow the renamed node**

| node | source_file | edges |
|---|---|---|
| `firmware_lib_portal` (kept) | `firmware/lib/portal.py` | 16 |
| `firmware_lib_portal_html` (new) | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | **0** |

In the cache, the HTML node has three `references` edges to card nodes on the same page. With the PR, those edges still start from the `.py` node, exactly as on the baseline.

The cause is a path-form mismatch. Semantic nodes and edges reach `build()` with an **absolute** `source_file`. I confirmed this for a cache hit: `load_cached` re-anchors them to absolute (`cache.py` ~1138-1142, "the same absolute-path shape that a fresh in-process extraction produces"). Before calling `deduplicate_entities`, `build()` makes only the **node** `source_file` repo-relative (`build.py` ~1757-1760 in 0.9.84). Edges stay absolute until `build_from_json` runs after dedup. `_disambiguate_defining_collisions` keys renames on `(id, node source_file)` and looks edges up by `(endpoint, edge source_file)`, so no edge ever matches. The new unit tests call `deduplicate_entities` directly, with nodes and edges sharing one relative path, so they don't cover this. Comparing normalised paths in the rename, or normalising edge `source_file` in `build()` before dedup, should fix it. A test that goes through `build()` with absolute paths would catch it.

**Problem 2: the doc case yields an orphan near-duplicate**

| node | source_file | edges |
|---|---|---|
| `docs_firmware_protocol` (existing) | `docs/firmware/protocol.md` | 7 |
| `docs_firmware_protocol_md` (new) | `docs/firmware/protocol.md` | **0** |

- The new test expects `docs_firmware_protocol`, but on a real corpus that ID already belongs to the file's own document node. The fallback therefore gives `docs_firmware_protocol_md`: a second node for the same file.
- The dropped node ("protocol (top-level)") is not a separate entity. It is the firmware doc's wikilink to the top-level `docs/protocol.md`, and its only edge (`docs_firmware_protocol references protocol`) already resolves to that document's node. Restoring it creates an orphan duplicate, and for this case the old drop was arguably the right outcome. My issue overstated this case, sorry about that. The genuine loss is the extension case (`x.py` / `x.html`).

**Suggestion**

- Keep the rename for the "same stem, different extension" case, but make edges follow it under the path forms `build()` actually passes to dedup.
- For a bare ID that only collides because a file *refers* to another file's entity, merging into the existing node (or skipping it) may be better than minting a new one.

Still present in **0.9.82** (PyPI `graphifyy`, macOS, Python 3.14), reached through the Claude Code skill's Part B/C with subagents and no API key.

- `build.py:42` is unchanged (`_AST_LOC_RE = re.compile(r"^L\d")`), and `watch.py:2331` still writes with `to_json(..., force=True)`.
- Corpus: a mixed Markdown vault plus one vendored Python package. The only change since the last build was a version bump of that package (67 code files).
- One `graphify update .` dropped **1,604 node IDs from 88 files**. Outside the bumped package, **882 IDs were lost**: 685 Markdown nodes stamped `_origin: "ast"` by an earlier build's shape fallback, and 182 Markdown nodes with no `_origin` but an `L<line>` location. **Every one of the 867 had an `L<line>` `source_location`**, and most were `concept` or `rationale` nodes, which no Markdown AST pass can emit.
- The same run re-clustered and renamed all 442 labelled communities by their hub, so only 67 of 7,199 surviving nodes kept their label.
- The template in `skill.md` does say `"source_location": null`. Our subagents wrote line numbers anyway, so the template alone does not prevent this. A tier check that also uses `file_type` (or stamps `_origin: "semantic"` at merge time) would.

Workaround we used: restore the pre-update `graphify-out/`, then re-extract only the changed code files with `extract()` and merge them into `graph.json` with communities frozen, replacing only `_origin == "ast"` nodes whose `source_file` is one of those files.

> this-field lookup falls back to the file-wide type table, defeating per-class disambiguation
> Fields of anonymous class expressions are no longer typed

Both confirmed and fixed in 02f73558.

1. The fallback was real: constructor parameter properties of every class in a file still lived in the file-wide table, so `A.run` could read `B`'s `constructor(private repo: RepoB)`. `this.x` in a method of a known class now reads only that class and its bases, never the file table. To keep that complete, the class's fields now also come from parameter properties, `this.x = param` / `this.x = new T()` in the constructor, and `get x(): T` / `set x(v: T)`; a field declared on a base class is found through `inherits` (its type judged by the declaring file's imports), and static fields are kept apart and read only from static methods.
2. Fields of an unnamed class (`export default class { .. }`) go to the file table again, which its class-less methods still read, as on 0.9.84.

Fields now live on the class node (`_ts_fields`, `_ts_static_fields`); a changed-files rebuild forwards them with the unchanged files' import edges, so an inherited field resolves as in a full build (NestJS, changing `nest-application.ts` / `module-ref.ts`: 2195 / 2195 / 2195).

One remaining edge case: `key()` calls `_rank_path`, which resolves a *relative* path against the CWD. Node paths are already root-relative at that point, so when graphify is started from a subdirectory of the scan root, node and edge keys no longer match and the edges stay on the `.py` node. On our corpus, `da923e9` started from a subdirectory gives the html node 0 edges again. With the patch below it is identical to a run from outside the root.

The patch only relativizes absolute paths in `key()`. It also tidies the extension comparison, which was one 254-character line (a lost line continuation?), and adds a regression test that fails on `da923e9`:

+def _extension(source_file: str) -> str:
+    """The lowercased extension of ``source_file`` (``.html``), or ``""`` if it has none."""
+    m = _EXTENSION.search(source_file.replace("\\", "/"))
+    return m.group(0).lower() if m else ""
