Investigated this round's 5 findings (matching 93a961b).

Confirmed real, fixed in fd4893d: "Fixed heredoc delimiter allows command injection via saved answer text". The save result answer heredoc, and the ingest url/author/contributor heredocs added earlier in this branch, all closed on a bare `EOF`. Each one captures free text the model itself wrote or lifted from a fetched page, and a line that is just `EOF` is entirely plausible boilerplate inside such text (quoting shell output, a log excerpt, a code fence label) — that closes the heredoc early and lets the rest of the captured text execute as shell commands, exactly the class of bug the heredoc was introduced to prevent. Gave each one its own distinctive delimiter (`GRAPHIFY_ANSWER_EOF`, `GRAPHIFY_URL_EOF`, `GRAPHIFY_AUTHOR_EOF`, `GRAPHIFY_CONTRIBUTOR_EOF`), matching the `GRAPHIFY_ROOT_EOF` pattern Step 1's own scan root heredoc already uses for the same reason, across every host.

Investigated and found to be a false positive: "Quoted .graphify_python no longer supports interpreter commands with arguments". `.graphify_python` is always written as `sys.executable` (Step 1, `"$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', ...).write(sys.executable)"`), which is a single absolute path to the interpreter binary, never a multi word command with its own arguments — it is the exact scenario the quoting fix on this branch exists to handle (a path containing a space), not a case the quoting breaks.

Investigated and found to be a false positive: "Skill now calls to_json with new force kwarg without enforcing compatible graphify version". The skill markdown is generated from, and shipped together with, the exact graphify release that defines `to_json`'s `force` parameter — `graphify install` always writes the skill matching the installed package, and the README's existing "Skill version mismatch warning" guidance already covers the one way these could drift apart (an old skill file left over from before an upgrade). There is no code path where a skill file calling `force=` ships paired with a `to_json` that lacks it.

The remaining two findings ("User supplied INPUT_PATH can trigger shell command substitution", "INPUT_PATH Python literal escaping remains injectable") restate the same inherent limitation already addressed and explained in earlier rounds on this PR: INPUT_PATH is substituted into prompt text the agent itself interprets before any code runs, so the mitigation is necessarily an instruction (quote escaping, forward slashes), not a runtime enforcement — there is no code boundary left to add a hard guard at once the value is already in the markdown the model reads. The existing instruction (escape a literal single quote as `\'`, substitute Windows paths with forward slashes) is the practical mitigation for this category, same as Step 1's own forward slash instruction. No code change made for these two.

Investigated both findings from this round (matching b603ad0), both real, fixed in 44f0cd7.

- "Fence tracking closes on the wrong fence delimiter": the scan toggled a single `in_fence` boolean on ANY fence line, backtick or tilde, treating the two as interchangeable. CommonMark closes a fence only on a line of the SAME character it opened with, so a tilde fenced example that itself demonstrates a backtick fence as literal documentation text had that backtick line wrongly treated as closing the outer fence. A heading line still logically inside the tilde fence would then end the scan early — exactly the data loss shape this file exists to prevent. Added a small `_toggle_fence` helper that tracks which character opened the current fence and only closes on a matching one.

- "boundary_prefix matched via lines[j].startswith (raw) vs stripped for other checks": confirmed, the boundary_prefix check matched the raw line while the ATX heading regex right beside it in the same condition matched the stripped line. A sibling heading indented by a couple of spaces is still a real ATX heading per CommonMark, so the raw line check missed it as a boundary even though the stripped check would have caught the exact same line a moment later. Switched it to match the stripped line, consistent with every other check in the same scan.

Both fixes verified against the pre-fix code first (confirmed each new regression test actually fails without the fix, not just that it passes with it), with the fence test specifically needing an unbalanced single inner fence line rather than a balanced pair — a balanced pair's toggle parity happens to cancel out and masks the bug even on the old code.

Field report: we merged this PR (head `bd4c524`) onto current `v8` (0.9.85) in our fork and measured it on three private PHP codebases (Symfony 8 / PHP 8.4-8.5, Laravel 12), 42k to 450k lines. Short version: large recall gain, no wrong edge found in any sample.

## Merge onto 0.9.85

The merge is on [`alexwrite/graphify@integrate/php-lawnstarter`](https://github.com/alexwrite/graphify/tree/integrate/php-lawnstarter) (a merge, not a rebase). Four conflicts, one in code:

- `graphify/extract.py`, cross-file pass: your PHP function-call filter (`php_function_call` / `_is_php_function_target`) and upstream's widened C# guard (`csharp_new or lang == "csharp"`, #4245) touch the same spot. Both kept, PHP filter first. They compose because both only remove candidates.
- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` / `CHANGELOG.md`: kept 0.9.85, moved your section above 0.9.85 as `Unreleased`.

One thing to flag for your next rebase: the PR relies on the 0.9.80 -> 0.9.81 bump to roll the version-namespaced AST cache. Upstream is now past 0.9.81, so keeping the upstream version would replay pre-fix PHP facts from any 0.9.85 cache. We bumped `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` from 7 to 8 instead, which is the mechanism `cache.py` documents for this case and does not depend on the version number.

Gates on the merge: `pytest tests/ -q` **7498 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed**; `ruff check .` clean; the five `tools.skillgen` CI checks pass; `bandit -r graphify -ll` identical to `v8` (12 findings, same rules). `pyright` goes from 607 to 617 errors, all in families already present on `v8` (Optional keys, and the per-language `receiver_types` union pyright cannot narrow through `config.ts_module`); pyright is not a CI gate upstream.

## Measurements (`extract --code-only`, same frozen snapshot before and after)

| | Symfony, ~450k lines | Laravel, ~155k lines | Symfony, ~42k lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calls` edges whose source is a PHP node | 17,448 -> 31,523 | 5,212 -> 5,439 | 2,352 -> 2,940 |
| of which INFERRED | 783 -> 15,046 | 777 -> 1,104 | 106 -> 746 |
| `indirect_call` (first-class callables) | 0 -> 14 | 0 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| Inbound `calls` to one heavily injected class (a repository / a model / a repository) | 34 -> 175 | 110 -> 161 (to methods: 21 -> 72) | 0 -> 1 |
| Distinct caller files of those methods | 1 -> 72 | 1 -> 14 | 0 -> 1 |

On the first codebase, the 34 "before" edges were all calls from inside the class itself: no external caller was visible. On the third, the one edge is the only real caller (grep-verified).

**Recall check** (first codebase, target class above): 96 call sites go through a property typed with that class. 93 get an edge on their own line; 2 more are deduplicated (same caller/callee pair already linked on another line); **1 is a genuine miss: the call sits inside a closure** (`$this->cache->get(KEY, function () { ... $this->repo->count() ... })`). Minimal repro, generic names:

```php
class Stats {
    public function __construct(private Repo $repo) {}
    public function direct(): int { return $this->repo->countAll(); }                        // edge, INFERRED 0.85
    public function viaClosure(callable $c): int { return $c(function (): int { return $this->repo->countAll(); }); } // no edge
    public function viaArrow(): array { return array_map(fn ($x) => $this->repo->findActive(), [1]); }              // no edge
}
```

The closure is a caller node (`{closure#1}`) and its direct `$this->m()` calls do resolve; only the property type does not seem to reach it. Not a wrong edge, just a missing one, and probably worth a follow-up since cache/collection/transaction callbacks are everywhere in Symfony and Laravel code.

## Precision check

- **New edges**: 60 sampled at random among edges present after and absent before (seed `20261011`, 20 per codebase; populations 14,808 / 651 / 642). Each one checked by reading the call site, the receiver's declaration in the enclosing method (property, promoted param, typed param, `$x = new T`), the `use` import, and the target method. **60/60 correct.** Every sampled edge was INFERRED 0.85, including `(new T())->m()` without a written namespace, consistent with the PR description.
- **Untyped receivers**: every `$this->p->m()` with an untyped `p`, and every `$v->m()` with an untyped, never-reassigned parameter, **whose method name exists on some in-corpus class** (so a decoy is always available): 39 sites across the three codebases, **0 edges** on any of those lines.
- **Removed edges** (733 / 424 / 54): a seeded sample of 18 were all wrong before the merge: `parent::__construct()` bound to an unrelated enum's `parent()` method, `parent::tearDown()` likewise, same-file self-loops where `$this->dependency->create()` bound to the caller's own `create()`, and the `request()` / `route()` / `redirect()` helpers and the `file()` builtin bound to methods of unrelated classes.

## Observations outside this PR

- The documented same-file residual exists in the wild: a private method named like a global helper and wrapping it (`private function round_x(...) { return round_x($v, 2); }`) yields a method self-loop at EXTRACTED instead of an edge to the function.
- `Foo::bar()` binds to the class node, never to the method `bar`, even when `bar` is a declared static method (777 and 1,919 such sites on the two larger codebases). Pre-existing extractor behaviour (`callee = scope name`), unchanged by this PR; the `PhpNameResolver` / `_php_class_fqns` machinery here looks like the right base to bind these to the method.

Thanks for the refuse-don't-guess discipline: on these codebases it is what makes the new edges usable without a second check.

@L4XB here is exactly what L4XB/graphify#1 proposes on top of this branch. Each item can be taken or dropped on its own.

**1. Call-specific hint on a firing nudge** (`graphify/cli.py`: `_search_hint_terms`, `_graph_hint`, `_with_hint`)
Your `_nudge_allowed` budget decides when a nudge fires. When it does, the nudge (and the strict-mode deny) now ends with a ready command and up to five graph nodes:
```
Start with: `graphify explain "load_config()"`
What the graph already has for this call:
- load_config() (src/app.py L10)
```
- **Search:** the terms come from the Grep `pattern`, or the pattern argument of `grep`/`rg`/`ag`/`ack`. Value-taking flags such as `-t`/`-g`/`-A` are skipped. `find`/`fd` are excluded because they match file names, not content.
- **Read:** the hint lists the file's symbols in line order and suggests `graphify explain "<file>"`.
- **Ranking:** labels only. Exact matches come first and suggest `explain`; otherwise it suggests `query`. Terms shorter than 5 characters only match exactly, so `src` does not list every path.
- **Cost and safety:** it scans `graph.json` labels directly (0.3–0.5 s on 3k–15k-node graphs) instead of loading the query stack (~1.5 s). Graphs over 24 MiB, a malformed graph, no match, or any error all return your nudge unchanged. Graph text is one line, with no control characters or backticks, and capped in length, since `graph.json` is repository content.

**2. Narrower nudge wording** (`_SEARCH_NUDGE`, `_READ_NUDGE`, `_READ_DENY`)
"…or to modify/debug specific lines" excused almost every targeted read in practice. Raw reads are now allowed "only once you know the exact file and lines you need, from the graph or an earlier read".

**3. Always-on rule** (Claude, AGENTS.md and Gemini blocks; recorded as a sanctioned edit `_QUERY_FIRST_EDIT` in `tools/skillgen/gen.py`)
"For codebase questions, first run `graphify query`…" becomes "…before your first grep, search or source-file read for a codebase question, and put this rule in every subagent prompt that explores code. Read raw files only for lines the graph or an earlier read already located." The Kiro and Antigravity blocks are unchanged.

**Why:** in our downstream build, agents still skipped the nudge within the budget. In session logs, a reminder got 28–41 deliveries per session against 0–2 `graphify` calls, and the model's reasoning never mentioned it. The hint shows what the graph has instead of only asking. Smoke on a real repo: `rg 'stripHiddenWrappers'` now gets `graphify explain "stripHiddenWrappers()"` plus its file and line.

**Branch notes:** it first merges current `v8`, as you did in `d7ba4af`. The README conflict was resolved to `v8`'s side, because the strict-mode note moved to the docs site. Tests in `tests/test_hook_guard.py` and `tests/test_hook_strict.py` cover hints, ranking, the 5-node cap, flag parsing, hostile and malformed graphs, the size cap and the deny hint. The skillgen guards pass. We carry this downstream until it lands. If you'd rather keep this PR to the budget, I can open it upstream as a separate PR stacked on this one.

> Incremental rebuild can preserve stale import edges

They cannot reach the graph. `watch.py` forwards only edges whose `source_file` is an unchanged, live file (`ctx_live`, the same scoping as the `contains` / `method` / `inherits` edges already forwarded), and `extract()` keeps only the edges the resolvers add on top (`all_edges.extend(_rl_edges[_e0:])`), so a forwarded import edge is evidence for the gate and never output. An import edge of an unchanged file is current for that file; if its target moved, the gate fails exactly as in a full build.

Pinned in 46dfd9ce: `test_rebuild_after_the_imported_class_moves_matches_a_full_build` (the unchanged conftest.py still imports `CliRunner` from `app.testing`, which no longer defines it; the fixture call stays unlinked in both builds). Writing it showed one other difference, the same on clean 0.9.85: the unchanged conftest's own `CliRunner()` call is not re-resolved to the moved class on a changed-files rebuild (#3570), so the test compares the fixture arm's edges.

The coupling note on `_resolve_python_member_calls`: the new callee is the `_nearest_fixture` lookup the arm needs; the arm itself mirrors the typed-receiver arm next to it.

Here's how I'm planning to fix this. Happy to change course if you'd prefer something else.

The core problem is that INPUT_PATH and LABELS_DICT get pasted into the Python scripts as text. Wrapping the scripts in heredocs would stop the shell from running `$(...)`, but a label with a `'` in it could still break out of the Python string. The Windows skill already uses here-strings and has the same hole, so I'd rather remove the pasting altogether.

What I'd change:

- INPUT_PATH: Step 1 already saves the resolved root to graphify-out/.graphify_root. The later steps and the --update runbook would read it from there, using a small helper with the same in-repo check hooks.py does. No path gets pasted anywhere.
- LABELS_DICT: the agent writes the labels to a JSON file through a quoted heredoc, and Step 5 loads it with json.loads. A weird label just fails to parse.
- Item 5: add quotes around $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python).
- IS_DIRECTED stays as it is, since it's only True or False and comes from the user's own flag.

The earlier fixes (#3642, #3742, #3844) only covered Step 1 and --watch, and nothing caught the other steps. So I'd also make skillgen refuse to render a skill that pastes INPUT_PATH or LABELS_DICT into a script, and add tests that run the generated blocks with a hostile path and label.

Windows is generated from the bash fragments, so it gets the same fix.

I'll leave items 3 and 4, and converting the scripts to heredocs, for later PRs.

Thanks @Mpasha17! The single-file case (#4334) is fixed correctly. One thing before this can land: the guard fires on *any* referenced name whose bare slug equals the file stem — including a same-named class that's **imported** into the file rather than defined in it. For a file in a subdirectory that does `from .base import Widget` and only uses `Widget`, the redirect returns a local qualified id for which no node is ever created (dangling edge) and it suppresses the sourceless stub the cross-file rewire relies on — a regression, and that path is untested.

Could you gate the redirect on the name actually being a *local* definition (e.g. only redirect when the qualified id ends up in `seen_ids` at end-of-walk, otherwise fall through to the sourceless stub), and add a test for the imported-same-name-in-a-subdirectory case? Happy to point at the exact spot if useful.

Your extracted `_render_query` is based on the pre-fix body, so a mechanical rebase would silently drop `seeds=start_nodes` and regress seed-first/truncation for both seeded and keyword queries.

Thanks for the detailed report. Two related observations from our own review that might help prioritise the fix:

1. #3803 narrows the section boundary, which is the right fix for this report. Independently of that, there is still no safety net when a bug of this class hits again: `install`/`uninstall` rewrite `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (and the user-global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) without keeping a copy. `settings.json` already gets a rolling `<name>.graphify-bak` (`_write_settings_with_backup`, #2167) and `SKILL.md` gets a `.bak` (#3144), so the same single-copy approach for the instruction files would turn a data-loss bug into a recoverable one. #1310 contains a backup helper for exactly this, if that PR is revived.
2. `claude_uninstall` still looks only at the project directory (`install.py` `md_targets`), so a global install leaves its block in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` pointing at a deleted skill; that is #3573.

A regression test for the "foreign content after the block" shape could use: a file with only `##` headings after the block, a file with another tool's marker block after it, and a CRLF file - all three must come back byte-identical except for the graphify block.

I've pushed a fix for the review finding at `julia.py:199` (functor receiver falling back to the variable name), and I reproduced it before fixing it. A module-qualified type is a `field_expression`, which the operand filter skipped:

| Definition | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `(b::Mod.Box)(x)` | `(b)()` ❌ | `(Box)()` |
| `(b::Mod.Box{T})(x) where T` | dropped ❌ | `(Box)()` |
| `(::Mod.Box)(x)` | dropped ❌ | `(Box)()` |

The functor branch now reads the typed expression's last child, which is always the type, through a new `_functor_type_name`. It unwraps `Box{T}`, `Mod.Box` and `A.B.Box`, and returns `None` for anything else. It never falls back to another identifier.

`test_julia_qualified_functor_uses_type_not_variable` covers these cases and fails without the fix. All 467 tests in `tests/test_languages.py` pass.

Took a proper look at this rather than going off the description, because the "Grok can't use Graphify" framing didn't match what I expected. Installed Grok Build 1.0.50 on Windows and ran current Graphify (no grok support) against it.

Short version: Grok already discovers Graphify today through its Claude-compatibility layer. What's actually broken is narrower, and this PR fixes it.

## 1) Discovery already works

Install current Graphify the normal way:

```
graphify install --platform claude --project
```

Then ask Grok what it loads:

```
grok --trust inspect
```

It reports the graphify skill, the CLAUDE.md instructions, and the PreToolUse hooks:

```
Project Instructions (3)   -> CLAUDE.md + .claude/CLAUDE.md (graphify section)
Skills                     -> graphify   project [claude]
Hooks                      -> pre_tool_use  Bash|Grep  -> graphify hook-guard search
                              pre_tool_use  Read|Glob  -> graphify hook-guard read
```

Grok's own docs confirm it scans `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills` by default, and reads `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Since `graphify install` defaults to the claude platform, a normal install already lands where Grok looks. So `graphify update .` / `graphify query` and the skill already work in Grok before this PR.

## 2) The hooks load but don't fire (the real bug this PR fixes)

`_run_hook_guard` reads `tool_input` / `tool_name` / `session_id` (cli.py:909, 1041) and `file_path` (cli.py:929). Grok sends `toolInput` / `toolName` / `sessionId`, and `read_file` carries `target_file`. Feeding both shapes to the real command:

```
Claude-shaped {"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"grep -r x ."},"session_id":"s"} -> emits the "MANDATORY ... graphify query" nudge
Grok-shaped   {"toolName":"run_terminal_command","toolInput":{"command":"grep -r x ."},"sessionId":"s"} -> prints nothing
```

So the PR's "before this change, hook-guard printed nothing for a Grok-shaped payload" checks out.

## 3) The skill assumes Claude's Agent tool

The semantic-extraction step mandates `subagent_type="general-purpose"` (skill-*.md:216, 296). Grok's subagent API differs, so the LLM pass as written is Claude-specific. That's exactly the "sequential" rendering this PR adds. (I couldn't run that end to end, no Grok login here, so it's read from code, not executed.)

## Overall

Worth landing, but the problem statement oversells it. It isn't "Grok can't use Graphify". It's "Grok picks Graphify up through Claude compat, but the hooks no-op because the payload is camelCase and the semantic step assumes Claude's Agent tool, so a native grok path makes it work properly instead of by accident". That framing is more accurate and easier for a maintainer to merge.

Caveats: verified on Windows with Grok 1.0.50 (the PR tested 1.0.46); discovery confirmed via `grok inspect`, agent/subagent behavior not executed (no login).

1. **Nested type paths cached by colliding node id: confirmed.** Two same-named nested types under different outers

   `if rc.get("is_member_call"): continue`, before the own-type branch; only a bare `M()` reaches it. Their targets

3. **Shadowed-base pruning by bare label: confirmed.** A half naming `Other.IFoo`, or `IFoo` through a `using` alias,
   lost its placeholder edge next to `App.IFoo`. Fixed in 37ec971: only a bare-name placeholder is dropped; one whose

### Follow-up: two more concrete issues found while using the workaround

After patching `DOC_EXTENSIONS` locally as described above and running a full extraction over the ABAP Cloud + CAP corpus, I hit two more bugs — one a second concrete instance of the "silently produces zero nodes" failure mode, the other a provenance/merge-correctness bug that's a direct violation of invariant #2 in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("a real source-backed record must not lose to a richer sourceless stub").

**1. `.json` files with no package-manifest shape silently produce zero nodes, even though `.json` is already in `CODE_EXTENSIONS`.**

Two abapGit ATC-check-configuration files (`*.chkc.json`, `*.chko.json` — small, real JSON config objects, not manifests) were present in `manifest.json` with populated hashes, `classify_file()` correctly returned `CODE` for them, `_is_sensitive()` correctly returned `False` — yet they produced zero nodes anywhere in `graph.json`. Root cause: `.json` routes to the AST path, but there's no AST parser for arbitrary non-manifest JSON, so Part A silently emits nothing for them, and because their content never changed, incremental `--update` never routed them to the semantic (document) path either — they're permanently stuck with no extraction path. I worked around it locally the same way as the extensions above: a compound-extension special case (mirroring the existing `.blade.php` check in `classify_file()`) routing `*.chkc.json`/`*.chko.json` to `DOCUMENT`. The general version of this bug: **any `.json` file that isn't a recognized package manifest has no extraction path at all** — worth either giving `.json` a minimal generic-JSON AST extractor, or falling back to `DOCUMENT` for `.json` files that `is_package_manifest_path()` rejects.

**2. Duplicate node-ID collisions during merge keep whichever record arrived first, not the most authoritative one — silently discarding real source-backed content in favor of a thin external-reference stub.**

Two parallel extraction chunks independently derived the *same* deterministic node id for one real CDS table (one chunk read the actual `.tabl.xml` source; a different, earlier-processed chunk only saw the table named in another file's `.baseinfo` sidecar and created a lightweight external-reference stub under the same id). The merge step (`seen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}; for n in sem['nodes']: if n['id'] not in seen: ...`) kept whichever node was encountered first and silently dropped the real one — with no warning, since both candidates are individually valid nodes. Separately, I hit the same failure mode manually while fixing an unrelated duplicate-node problem: when merging two nodes that legitimately share an id, filling only empty fields on the "kept" node (instead of preferring whichever source is more authoritative) let a thin ADT-metadata-sidecar node win over the real `.abap`-source node for the same function module, silently erasing its real source attribution.

Both are instances of the same gap: node-id collision handling has no concept of "which source is more authoritative," so richness/provenance can lose on ordering alone — exactly what invariant #2 in `CONTRIBUTING.md` says must not happen. A fix might log a warning (or require an explicit reconciliation rule) whenever two extraction fragments produce the same node id with different `source_file`/richness, rather than resolving it by insertion order.

Happy to share the exact repro file shapes for either of these if useful for a regression test fixture.

Root cause and a fix for this, checked against `v8` at a5ba60d (0.9.86). Fix with regression tests: #4369.

### Root cause (`graphify/extractors/powershell.py`)

1. **Dot-source (around L264-L280).** The path is read only from a `command_name` child of `command_name_expr`. tree-sitter-powershell parses the common forms differently:
   - `. ./lib.ps1`, `. .\lib.ps1` -> `command_name` (handled)
   - `. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"`, `. '.\lib.ps1'` -> `string_literal` (skipped)
   - `. $PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1` -> `path_command_name` (skipped)
   - `. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "lib.ps1")` -> `parenthesized_expression` (runtime-only path)
2. **Script-scope calls (L415-L416).** `walk_calls` runs only over `function_bodies`, so commands in a script's main body never become `calls` edges or `raw_calls`. Calls inside functions do resolve across files, which is why this looked partial.

### Minimal repro

```text
repro/
  lib.ps1    function Helper { 'hi' }
  main.ps1   . "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"
             Helper
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extractors.powershell import extract_powershell
r = extract_powershell(Path("repro/main.ps1"))
print([e for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "imports_from"])  # [] on 0.9.86
print(r["raw_calls"])                                               # [] on 0.9.86, Helper is missing
```

Variant results on 0.9.86 / with #4369:

| Dot-source form | 0.9.86 | #4369 |
|---|---|---|
| `. ./lib.ps1`, `. .\lib.ps1` | edge | edge |
| `. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"` | none | edge |
| `. $PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1` | none | edge |
| `. '.\lib.ps1'` | none | edge |
| `. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "lib.ps1")` | none | none (known limit) |

### The fix in #4369

- Accept `command_name`, `path_command_name` and `string_literal` and strip surrounding quotes. The existing basename logic does the rest.
- Also call `walk_calls(root, file_nid, None)`. `walk_calls` already stops at `function_statement`/`class_statement`, so function bodies are not walked twice; a control test covers this.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 8 -> 9, so cached results for unchanged `.ps1` files are refreshed.

The new tests fail on `v8` (4 of 5; the 5th is the no-duplication control) and pass with the fix. Full suite and lint results are in the PR description. Prepared with Claude Code on my behalf.

Thanks for the review. I looked at both advisory findings, and neither needs a code change:

- **`Promise.withResolvers` is Node 22+ (`graphify/pi/index.ts:98`).** The extension only runs inside its host. Pi declares `"engines": {"node": ">=22.19.0"}`, and Oh My Pi runs on Bun, which also provides `Promise.withResolvers`. No supported host lacks it.
- **`graphify pi guard install` runs the `pi` that `PATH` resolves (`graphify/install.py:2595`).** This is intentional. The command is user-invoked and does the same thing as typing `pi install <dir>`. It uses `shutil.which`, the lookup Graphify already uses for `opencode`, `gws` and `claude`. The strict rule against project-local executables applies to the extension, because it runs automatically on every tool call, possibly inside an untrusted repository. The extension enforces that rule: it only uses a `graphify` on an absolute `PATH` entry outside the project, and the tests cover it.
